shots.name: Green Tea Shot

shots.name: B-52
shots.taste: Coffee, cream and orange in three distinct layers.
shots.garnish: No garnish
shots.note: Three-layer house pour using orange cognac liqueur (Grand Marnier). The reference uses orange liqueur; test the layering with your venue’s actual bottles.
steps: Chill a clear shooter glass and the measured ingredients; do not put ice in the glass.
Measure each liqueur into its own small pouring vessel so you can control the flow.
Pour the coffee liqueur down the inside wall to form the base.
Hold the back of a barspoon close to the base layer and trickle the Irish cream onto it; raise the spoon as the level rises.
Move the clean spoon just above the cream and slowly float the orange cognac liqueur over it.
Inspect the three bands and serve the glass upright without stirring.
shots.upgrade: Pre-chilled bottles and a controlled spoon pour for three distinct bands.
shots.techniqueTip: A long drop disturbs the lower layer. Keep the spoon near the surface; actual bottle densities determine how well layers hold.
